historical_evidence: `3a DF` extract separates embedded CfD from energy and backwardation; support reconciliation evidence exists separately.
current_2030_treatment: Balancing (post-curtailment) dispatch settled against published allocation-round clearing prices in 2012 prices, indexed to the 2024 model basis by the ONS CPI annual-average ratio 133.9/96.1 = 1.393340, which reproduces DESNZ's own published 2012/2024 strike pairs for AR7 and AR7a. Recovered over CfD eligible supplier sales. A declared vintage schedule assigns allocation rounds to CP30 CfD capacity in proportion to the MW each round awarded for delivery by 2030/31, so offshore wind spans five distinct strikes from GBP52.04 (AR4) to GBP91.18 (AR7) rather than one; this takes effect only once the twelve monthly networks are rebuilt.
value_unit: GBP per 3100 kWh household ex VAT
proposed_method_and_gap: Remaining gaps: the vintage schedule gives a fleet-level contract mix, not site-level identity, because the CP30 fleet is synthetic. Until the rebuild, 100% of the gross payment still settles at the declared future strike and max_fallback_strike_share_of_payment stays unset. Within-round tranches that cleared at different prices (AR6 permitted reduction at 54.23, AR7 Scotland at 64.23) are not separated by a carrier-level schedule. Nuclear carries no CfD label and cannot: CP30 publishes nuclear as an unresolved national total (3,515 MW / 25,892 GWh) and the model spreads it across twenty buses as proxies, so Hinkley Point C can be neither identified nor ruled out. The exclusion is recorded and priced as a diagnostic: an HPC-strike CfD on the modelled 25.08 TWh would be about GBP1,644m a year, GBP17.09 per customer. Neither sizewell_c_rab (a RAB construction levy for a different station) nor nuclear_contract_counterparty (the counterparty body's own cost) covers it. The AR4 zero-payment-in-negative-hours term cannot be reproduced because the LP admits no negative bids.

value_unit: GBP per 3100 kWh household ex VAT
proposed_method_and_gap: Reconstruct levelisation and supplier recovery; forecast remaining accredited cohorts, generation/export payments, effective indexation and expiry. Do not add new projects merely because renewable capacity grows. [S7]

historical_evidence: Annex 4 row 15, multiplied by 3.1 MWh; station/ROC audits exist separately.
current_2030_treatment: Model-informed. Certificate volume is the ROC-eligible fleet still accredited in obligation year 2030/31 from the Ofgem accredited-stations register (22,853 MW of 42,444 MW; 19,591 MW has aged out of the 20-year window), multiplied by PyPSA balancing-stage carrier load factors and ROC banding, giving 54.5m ROCs. Valued at the notional ROC value (buy-out plus final recycle) restated in report prices, GBP75.95/ROC, and recovered over obligation-eligible supply. Reported under a declared Exchequer-relief case: GBP43.04 if the domestic relief ends in March 2029, GBP10.76 if it is extended, against the external reference of GBP17.
value_unit: GBP per 3100 kWh household ex VAT
proposed_method_and_gap: Remaining gaps: the fleet is the Ofgem register, not the model. The CP30 renewable fleet is synthetic (CP30_<carrier>_<n>, build_year 0, no accreditation dates), so no generator can hold a ROC label; WS5 step 1 would retain the operating fleet in CP30 integration and replace this route. Load factors are 2030 CP30 carrier averages applied to a legacy fleet, and biomass in particular runs below observed issuance. ROC banding is a carrier-level default that does not resolve accreditation vintage. The obligation-eligible supply denominator is identified with the CfD eligible-supply volume; both schemes exempt energy-intensive industry but their scopes are defined separately. Certificate supply is estimated, not reconciled to Ofgem issuance. The buy-out price needs no inflation forecast because it is RPI-indexed and therefore flat in real RPI terms.

historical_evidence: Detailed 2020 Annex 3 BSUoS extract and regional replay exist; 2024 maintained bundle retains network aggregate.
current_2030_treatment: Decomposed. bsuos_constraints is model-derived: accepted offer cost plus accepted bid cost plus the CfD curtailment compensation the balancing LP prices at a scalar zero, recovered over final demand and excluding VOLL-priced feasibility slack. bsuos_other_services is a NESO 2024-25 outturn residual of GBP5.1034/MWh of final demand, covering response, reserve, reactive, restoration, energy imbalance and NESO internal costs. The former flat GBP91 is retained as a reference only and is no longer summed into the bill.
value_unit: GBP per 3100 kWh household ex VAT
proposed_method_and_gap: Remaining gaps: modelled redispatch is cost against fixed wholesale positions, not NESO settlement expenditure. NESO's published 'Constraints' category covers all constraint actions, so the modelled thermal redispatch replacing it is narrower and the split is not exact. The non-constraint level is one outturn year held flat in real terms. WS8 would make the CfD balancing bid time-varying, turning the compensation term into a validation check rather than an addition.

historical_evidence: `3a DF` energy/backwardation/CfD detail and saved forward/spot procurement comparisons.
current_2030_treatment: Hourly model price weighted by a domestic consumption profile (Ofgem base/peak shaping input), rebased, with the shaping against system weighting shown as its own row. The single GBP52 procurement residual is replaced by four Ofgem-named allowances applied to the domestic energy cost: losses, transaction cost, day-ahead re-hedging and additional risk/basis, at observed 2020 intensities.
value_unit: GBP per 3100 kWh household ex VAT
proposed_method_and_gap: Remaining gaps: the domestic profile is Ofgem's two-block base/peak allocation, not an Elexon Profile Class 1 half-hourly regression, so within-block structure such as the post-19:00 domestic evening peak is absent. The forward premium stays at zero; the 1.460952 coefficient fitted on 2020 improves held-out 2024 forward-index error but is a chronological transfer test, not a prospective forward model. Procurement intensities are 2020 observations carried forward unchanged.
